fixes.explanation: Right, baker! “And Jehoahaz rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria.” (2 Kings 13:9) The passage says he reigned in Samaria seventeen years. So that's where he was laid to rest too. Same city for the throne and for the grave.

Yes, baker! “And his son Jehoash reigned in his place.” (2 Kings 13:9) The crown passed from Jehoahaz to his son. Jehoahaz was the son of Jehu, and now his own son takes the throne of Israel. Father to son, just like that.

That's it. “So the king put his hand on the bow, and Elisha put his hands on the king’s hands.” (2 Kings 13:16) The prophet's hands rested right on the king's hands as they held the bow. The king wasn't holding that bow alone. After that comes the east window and the shot.

Peace is a fine word, but Elisha doesn't use it here. He says, “This is the LORD’s arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram…” (2 Kings 13:17). Then he adds that the king will strike the Arameans in Aphek until he has put an end to them. That's a battle result, so the word that fits is the one Elisha said.

Yes, baker. “…they threw the man’s body into Elisha’s tomb.” (2 Kings 13:21) The Israelites had seen a band of raiders. Raiders in sight, so the body went into that tomb. Elisha had died and been buried, and that's where the man's body landed.
